source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.M2.N-RN.1: Standard is one sentence (rational exponent as radical). Skills spread over rational<->radical conversion, evaluation, why the exponent is a root, equivalent forms, simplifying, negative exponents, unknown exponent/base and error analysis. No cube roots of negatives; all bases are positive or x>=0 stated.
notes.NC17.M2.N-RN.2: Nth roots are written in words (cube root of x) because the converter has no nth-root sign; all radicands and bases are positive, so every answer is real and unique. Rationalizing denominators is left out of this set. Rationalizing denominators and irrational answers as numeric are left out; irrational results are choice questions. Radicals other than square roots are written in words (the cube root of ...).
notes.NC17.M2.N-RN.3: Mostly choice questions (explanations and proofs cannot be typed as numbers). A few D3 items go slightly beyond the four stated rules (sum/product of two irrationals can be rational) as the natural counter-cases; the zero exception to rational-times-irrational is tested on purpose. Full 69 written (23 per difficulty). Two-irrational sums/products (5) go slightly beyond the summary but are the natural contrast; every irrational used is named as irrational in the stem or is pi or a non-square root.
notes.NC17.M2.N-CN.1: Kept to what the summary names: i squared, powers of i, a + bi form, real and imaginary parts, equality, square roots of negatives. Arithmetic with two complex numbers (adding, multiplying a + bi forms, conjugates) is left for the standards that cover it. Questions on square roots of negatives use only the principal root; "which number squares to -25" never lists -5i among the options. Operations on complex numbers (addition, products of two complex numbers, conjugates) belong to later standards and are not asked; products such as 3i*2i appear only to show i squared is -1.
notes.NC17.M2.A-SSE.1: Interpretation is asked in words (what a term, factor, coefficient or whole bracket means) and by short calculations that need that reading; no graphs are referred to. Skills spread about evenly over quadratic terms, vertex form, factored form, square roots, inverse variation, right-triangle trigonometry and multi-part expressions.
notes.NC17.M2.A-SSE.3: Covers rewriting by completing the square and reading the minimum or maximum (and where it occurs); solving a quadratic equation by completing the square is a different standard and is not asked. Expressions as answers are choice questions; numeric answers are values.
notes.NC17.M2.A-APR.1: Division of polynomials is not part of this standard (only add, subtract, multiply), so it appears only as a factoring check. Closure is asked as a statement and through place-value checks at x = 10.
notes.NC17.M2.A-CED.2: Graphs are described in words (shape, vertex, start point, direction) or by table or point; answers needing irrational numbers or a drawn graph were not asked.
notes.NC17.M2.A-CED.3: Stated in text only: situations are written out, systems are written as pairs of equations. 16 choice (writing a system is naturally a choice), 14 numeric (solving a modeled system). Skills: write a linear system (2), solve a linear system from a story (5), write a linear-quadratic system (4), solve a linear-quadratic system (4), inverse variation write (4) and solve (4), square root write (2) and solve (2), interpret a solution (2), check a solution (1).
notes.NC17.M2.A-REI.2: Square root equations, inverse variation (y = k/x) and the extraneous solutions that squaring can create. Graphs and technology are not used. Where an equation with an extraneous root is asked as a number question, the question asks for the one valid (or the one extraneous) value so the key is unique.
notes.NC17.M2.A-REI.4: Text-only. 14 choice, 16 numeric. Answers with radicals or i-and-sqrt forms are choice questions. Skills: read a, b, c (2), discriminant (2), type of solutions from the discriminant (5), quadratic formula with real solutions (6), the imaginary unit (2), complex solutions a ± bi (6), product of a pair of complex solutions (1), completing the square / why the formula works (4), word problems (2).
notes.NC17.M2.A-REI.7: Text-only: tables are written out, graphs by their features, points or equations. 15 choice, 15 numeric. Skills: find the solution points (5), solve the quadratic that substitution gives (4), count the solutions (4), context (3 interpret, 4 solve), tables (3), graph features (3), check a point (3), set up the substituted equation (1). Solutions are exact (integers or simple fractions); the technology part of the standard (graphing) is covered by tables and described graphs.
notes.NC17.M2.A-REI.11: No graphs or technology are shown: intersections are given as points in words, or functions as small tables of values (rounded as stated), and the student reads the solution from them. Equations are square root and inverse variation, as in the summary.
notes.NC17.M2.F-IF.1: Rules are always given in the stem; points are written as coordinates and no figure is referred to. Numeric answers are single coordinates or sums, since a point cannot be typed as a number; point answers are choice questions.
notes.NC17.M2.F-IF.2: Dilations are centered at the origin and rotations about the origin, as the questions say; rotation directions are always stated. Figures are given by coordinates.
notes.NC17.M2.F-IF.4: Numbers: domain 6, range 6, rate of change 6, symmetry 6, end behavior 6. Graphs are given as tables, features in words or equations, since no picture can be shown.
notes.NC17.M2.F-IF.7: Graphs are never shown: features are asked from equations, short value tables or described graphs, all answerable by hand. Technology-based graphing is not tested.
notes.NC17.M2.F-IF.9: Representations used: equation, table of values, points, verbal description, and a graph described by its features (zeros, starting point, intercepts). No graphs shown. Quadratic minimum/maximum questions need the vertex by hand (x = -b/2a) or a given vertex form; all answers are exact whole numbers.
notes.NC17.M2.F-BF.1: Quadratics are built from zeros plus a point, or a described situation; inverse variation from a point, a table, ordered pairs or a story. Graphs are given by intercepts, vertex and points in words.
notes.NC17.M2.F-BF.3: Graphs are described in words and by tables of values; no picture is used. Functions are linear, quadratic, square root and inverse variation. Skills: vertical shift, horizontal shift, stretch/compression/reflection, effect on tables, effect on key features (vertex, asymptote, starting point), and picking the equation or the transformation. A few d3 questions combine two transformations.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.3: Polygons are described in words or by coordinates; no pictures are used. Counting questions say whether the 0 degree turn is included.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.4: Written entirely in text: every motion is described by its coordinates or its effect, no figures. Skills are the six named on each question; verifying by experiment is replaced by reasoning about what the motion keeps (lengths, angles, parallel and perpendicular lines, circles) and where points go.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.5: Figures are given as written-out coordinates. Rigid motions only (no dilations).
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.6: Figures are given by coordinates or side/angle data; no pictures. Image points are not named with primes (apostrophes), so images have new letters.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.7: Rigid motions are described by coordinates and words only; no figures. Transformations in the coordinate plane use whole-number coordinates.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.8: Triangles are described by their equal parts in words (no pictures). AAS is deliberately never used as a key or as the only way to tell options apart, since the summary lists ASA, SAS, SSS and HL. Rigid-motion justifications are asked as why-questions about a written argument.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.9: Thirty questions: vertical angles (5), angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal (7: alternate interior, corresponding, same-side interior, positions described in words), the perpendicular bisector (6, with coordinates and algebra), the angle bisector (6) and proofs asked as choice questions about a written argument (6). No figure is shown; every angle is placed in words or by point names. The converse of parallel-line theorems (proving lines parallel) is not asked.
notes.NC17.M2.G-CO.10: Thirty questions on the angle sum, exterior angles, isosceles base angles (and their converse) and the midsegment, with proof-reason questions asked as choices. Midsegment has the most questions (8) because it has the most forms (length, parallel angles, perimeter, coordinates). Full proofs are not asked, only the reasons and facts they use.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.1: The standard is about verifying properties by experiment; written here as using the properties (lengths, distances from the center, angles, parallel lines) on given numbers and coordinates. No figures are used.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.2: Coordinates of dilation images are kept to a few questions that also decide similarity (G-SRT.1 covers dilating lines and centers). A free-hand sketch or transformation drawing cannot be shown, so sequences are tested through vertices and radii given as coordinates.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.3: Both are choice or numeric; no picture is needed. Proofs are asked as choice questions about a written argument.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.4: Text-only: every triangle is given by its lettered points and lengths. Proof parts of the standard are asked as choice questions (a reason for a step, the next step, the first step of the Pythagorean proof). Pythagorean questions all use the altitude to the hypotenuse, so they need similarity and not just a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.6: Everything is by hand with Pythagorean triples; no calculator values and no angle measures beyond naming the angle. Ratios are asked as fractions.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.8: Angles are not found with inverse trigonometric keys (no calculator); angle questions ask for the correct equation, and side questions give the ratio value to use (e.g. tan 37 = 0.75) or use special angles with exact values.
notes.NC17.M2.G-SRT.12: Only the side ratios 1:1:sqrt(2) and 1:sqrt(3):2 are used, as the summary says; no trigonometric ratios. Answers with a square root are choice questions, so numeric ones are chosen to have whole-number answers (a leg from a hypotenuse written as k times sqrt(2), an area, a perimeter, a sum).
notes.NC17.M2.S-IC.2: Simulations are given as written results; the 2-standard-deviation rule or a range of simulated results is stated in each consistency question so there is one answer. Running a simulation itself cannot be done in text.
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.1: Probabilities are not asked (that belongs to later standards): events are described and counted as sets of outcomes. Outcomes are written out in words and lists, not as diagrams.
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.3: Tables are written out as lists of counts. Independence is tested by comparing P(A | B) with P(A); the product rule P(A and B) = P(A)P(B) is left to the next standard in the sequence (and to CP.4).
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.4: Tables are written out as lists of counts or percents, and raw data as a short list of people. Independence is tested by comparing P(A and B) with P(A)P(B) or P(A | B) with P(A).
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.5: Recognising and explaining conditional probability and independence is mostly conceptual, so about two thirds of the questions are choice questions. Numeric questions use independence to find a conditional probability or turn one into a count.
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.6: Finding a conditional probability is a calculation, so about two thirds of the questions are numeric. Choice questions cover interpretation and picking the right given group.
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.7: Numeric questions are the Addition Rule worked out; choice questions explain why the overlap is subtracted, when events can be added directly, and what P(A or B) means in context.
notes.NC17.M2.S-CP.8: Thirty questions across independent events, draws with and without replacement, the general rule with a conditional probability, finding a missing probability, and interpreting P(A and B). Probabilities are given as fractions or decimals; no tree or area diagrams are used.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: Which radical expression is equal to $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root: $x^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{x}$.

solve.work: x^(1/2) is the principal square root: sqrt(x).

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $64^{\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, and $\sqrt{64} = 8$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 27 cubic units. Its edge length is $27^{\frac{1}{3}}$ units. How long is the edge?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{3}$ means the cube root. Since $3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 = 27$, the edge is 3 units.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\sqrt{7}$?
questions.solution: The square root of 7 is $7^{\frac{1}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: Which of these is equal to $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{3}$ means the cube root.

solve.work: x^(1/3) is the cube root of x.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Since $\left(9^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^2 = 9^1 = 9$, the number $9^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is a positive number whose square is 9. What is $9^{\frac{1}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The positive number whose square is 9 is 3, so $9^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{9} = 3$.

solve.work: The positive number whose square is 9 is 3.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: The cube root of 125 is written as $125^{\frac{1}{n}}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: The cube root uses the exponent $\frac{1}{3}$, so $n = 3$.

solve.work: Cube root corresponds to exponent 1/3, so n = 3. (125^(1/3) = 5.)

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $81^{\frac{1}{4}}$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{4}$ means the fourth root. Since $3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 \cdot 3 = 81$, the value is 3.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: For $y \ge 0$, the square root of $y$ is written as $y^p$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: The square root is the exponent $\frac{1}{2}$, so $p = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the fifth root of $a$, for $a > 0$?
questions.solution: The fifth root uses the exponent $\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: $5^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot 5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ equals what whole number?
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1$, so the product is $5^{1} = 5$. This is why $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the square root of 5.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Which value of $a$ makes $\left(x^{a}\right)^{4} = x$ true for every $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $a \cdot 4 = 1$, so $a = \frac{1}{4}$. That is why $x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ is the fourth root of $x$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the cube root of $x$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: The cube root of $x$ is written $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: For $z \ge 0$, the expression $z^{\frac{1}{6}}$ is the $k$-th root of $z$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The denominator of the exponent is the index of the root, so $k = 6$.

solve.work: z^(1/6) is the 6th root of z, so k = 6.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: Tom wants to find $10^{\frac{1}{3}}$ on a calculator that has a cube root key but no exponent key. Which key should he use on the number 10?
choices: The key that finds square roots
The key that finds cube roots
The key that cubes a number
questions.answer: The key that finds cube roots
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{3}$ means the cube root, so he uses the cube root key on 10.

solve.answer: The key that finds cube roots

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A square tile has an area of 144 square centimeters. Its side length is $144^{\frac{1}{2}}$ centimeters. How long is each side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $144^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the square root of 144. Since $12 \cdot 12 = 144$, each side is 12 centimeters.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: A radical shows the eighth root of $w$, for $w \ge 0$. Written with a rational exponent it is $w^{\frac{1}{d}}$. What is $d$?
questions.solution: The index of the root is the denominator of the exponent, so $d = 8$.

solve.work: Eighth root of w = w^(1/8), d = 8.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which equation is true for every $x > 0$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, so $x^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{x}$. The others fail at $x = 16$: the square root is 4, but $16^{\frac{1}{4}} = 2$, $\frac{16}{2} = 8$ and $16^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the sixth root of 2?
questions.solution: The sixth root of 2 is $2^{\frac{1}{6}}$: the index 6 becomes the denominator of the exponent.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: In $x^{\frac{1}{n}}$, what does the denominator $n$ tell you to do to $x$?
questions.solution: A unit-fraction exponent $\frac{1}{n}$ means the $n$-th root, so the denominator tells you which root to take.

solve.work: x^{1/n} is the n-th root of x.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: The edge of a cube with volume $V$ is the cube root of $V$. Written with an exponent, the edge is $V^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: The cube root is the exponent $\frac{1}{3}$, so $p = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: Which radical expression is equal to $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, so $5^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{5}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent to radical
questions.stem: Maya writes $n^{\frac{1}{4}}$ as a radical expression, for $n \ge 0$. Which description is correct?
questions.solution: The denominator 4 of the exponent names the root, so $n^{\frac{1}{4}}$ is the fourth root of $n$.

solve.work: n^(1/4) is the fourth root of n.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Sam says $25^{\frac{1}{2}}$ means half of 25. Which value is actually equal to $25^{\frac{1}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, not half. $5 \cdot 5 = 25$, so $25^{\frac{1}{2}} = 5$.

questions.skill: Find the error in a rewrite
questions.stem: Lena says, "$x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ means $x$ divided by 3." Which statement corrects her?
choices: It is $x$ cubed, because the 3 is a power.
It is the cube root of $x$, not $x$ divided by 3.
It is $x$ multiplied by 3, because the exponent is a fraction.
It is the square root of $x$, because the exponent is less than 1.
questions.answer: It is the cube root of $x$, not $x$ divided by 3.
questions.solution: A unit-fraction exponent $\frac{1}{3}$ means the cube root: $\left(x^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{3} = x^{1} = x$.

solve.answer: It is the cube root of $x$, not $x$ divided by 3.
solve.work: x^(1/3) is the cube root of x.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: What is the value of $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when $x = 1000$?
questions.solution: $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x$. Since $10 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 1000$, the value is 10.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Which value is equal to $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root. Since $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$, the value is $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the square root of $x$, which is also $x^{0.5}$. Half of $x$ is a different expression.

solve.work: x^(1/2)=x^0.5=sqrt x = the square root of x; x/2 is not equal (e.g. x=4: 2 vs 2 equal, but x=9: 3 vs 4.5).

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $16^{\frac{1}{4}}$.
questions.solution: $16^{\frac{1}{4}}$ is the fourth root of 16. Since $2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 16$, the answer is 2.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Which equation shows that $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$?
questions.solution: $8^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the cube root of 8, the number that is a factor three times to make 8. Since $2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 8$, it is 2. (The other equations are false.)

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, $\left(x^{\frac{1}{5}}\right)^{5} = x^{k}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{1}{5} \cdot 5 = 1$, so $k = 1$. Using $x^{\frac{1}{5}}$ as a factor 5 times gives $x$, which is why it is the fifth root of $x$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: The radical expression $\sqrt{19}$ is rewritten as $19^{p}$. Which value of $p$ is correct?
questions.solution: A square root is an exponent of $\frac{1}{2}$, so $\sqrt{19} = 19^{\frac{1}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: Which radical expression is equal to $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: The denominator 3 is the root and the numerator 2 is the power: $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x^2$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: A student computes $8^{\frac{2}{3}}$ by finding the cube root of 8 and then squaring the result. What value does the student get?
questions.solution: The cube root of 8 is 2, and $2^2 = 4$, so $8^{\frac{2}{3}} = 4$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{3}$, for $x \ge 0$?

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Which statement best explains why $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the same as $\sqrt{5}$?
choices: Squaring $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ gives $5^{1} = 5$, so it is the positive number whose square is 5.
Multiplying 5 by $\frac{1}{2}$ gives 2.5, which is the square root of 5.
The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ tells us to divide 5 by 2 and then take the square.
Since $5^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot 5^{\frac{1}{2}} = 5^{\frac{1}{4}}$, the number $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is a fourth root.
questions.answer: Squaring $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ gives $5^{1} = 5$, so it is the positive number whose square is 5.
questions.solution: By the power of a power rule, $\left(5^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^2 = 5^{\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2} = 5^1 = 5$. The positive number whose square is 5 is $\sqrt{5}$, so $5^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{5}$.

solve.answer: Squaring $5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ gives $5^{1} = 5$, so it is the positive number whose square is 5.
solve.work: (5^(1/2))^2 = 5^1 = 5, so 5^(1/2) is the positive number whose square is 5, i.e. sqrt 5. Other options are false (2.5 is not sqrt 5; product gives 5^1, not 5^(1/4)).

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: A scientist models a quantity as $Q = t^{\frac{3}{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in hours. What is $Q$ when $t = 4$?

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the square root of $x^{5}$ can be written as $x^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: The square root is the exponent $\frac{1}{2}$, applied to $x^5$: $\left(x^5\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^{\frac{5}{2}}$. So $p = \frac{5}{2}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the expression $x^{\frac{5}{4}}$ equals the $n$-th root of $x^{5}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: In $x^{\frac{m}{n}}$ the denominator is the index of the root, so $n = 4$.

solve.work: x^(5/4) = fourth root of x^5, n = 4.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(y^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$, for $y \ge 0$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $6 \cdot \frac{1}{3} = 2$, so the result is $y^2$.

questions.skill: Find a base from a root
questions.stem: If $b^{\frac{1}{2}} = 6$ and $b$ is positive, what is $b$?
questions.solution: $b^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the square root of $b$. Squaring both sides gives $b = 6^2 = 36$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$ is the square root of $x^3$, which is also $\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^3$ and $x\sqrt{x}$. The cube root of $x^2$ is $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$, a different expression.

solve.work: x^(3/2) = (sqrt x)^3 = sqrt(x^3) = x * sqrt x. Cube root of x^2 = x^(2/3), which is not equal (e.g. x = 4: 8 vs about 2.52).

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Ben says $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$ equals $\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{3}$. Cai says it equals $\sqrt{x^{3}}$. Both use $x \ge 0$. Who is correct?
choices: Both are correct, since the order can be swapped.
Only Ben is correct, since the root must come first.
Only Cai is correct, since the power must come first.
Neither is correct, since the exponent is a fraction.
questions.answer: Both are correct, since the order can be swapped.
questions.solution: $x^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{3} = \left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{3}$ and also $x^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(x^{3}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{x^{3}}$.

solve.answer: Both are correct, since the order can be swapped.
solve.work: x^{3/2} = (x^{1/2})^3 = (x^3)^{1/2} for x ≥ 0; both forms are equal.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $16^{\frac{3}{4}}$.
questions.solution: The fourth root of 16 is 2, and $2^{3} = 8$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\left(25y^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$, for $y \ge 0$?
questions.solution: Apply the exponent to each factor: $25^{\frac{1}{2}} = 5$ and $\left(y^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = y$, so the result is $5y$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Evaluate $\sqrt{25^{3}}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $4^{\frac{5}{2}}$.
questions.solution: The square root of 4 is 2, and $2^{5} = 32$.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: The brightness of a lamp in a model is $B = d^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, where $d$ is the distance in meters. What is $B$ when $d = 25$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $25^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{25^{\frac{1}{2}}} = \frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: In a model, a planet's orbit takes $T = a^{\frac{3}{2}}$ days, where $a$ is its distance from its star in units. How many days is $T$ when $a = 9$?
questions.solution: $9^{\frac{3}{2}}$ is the square root of 9, cubed: $3^{3} = 27$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: For $t \ge 0$, $\left(\sqrt{t}\right)^{5} = t^{p}$. What is $p$?

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which exponent expression is equal to the cube root of $x^{4}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: The index 3 is the denominator and the power 4 is the numerator, so the cube root of $x^{4}$ is $x^{\frac{4}{3}}$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the fourth root of $7^{3}$?
questions.solution: The index 4 is the denominator and the power 3 is the numerator, so the fourth root of $7^{3}$ is $7^{\frac{3}{4}}$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the cube root of $x^{4}$ equals $x$ times the cube root of $x^{k}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: $x^{\frac{4}{3}} = x^{1 + \frac{1}{3}} = x \cdot x^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x^{1}$. So $k = 1$.

solve.work: Cube root of x^4 = cube root of (x^3·x) = x·cube root of x, so k = 1.

questions.skill: Find the error in a rewrite
questions.stem: Dev says $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the square root of $x^{3}$, for $x \ge 0$. What is wrong with his statement?
choices: Nothing is wrong, because the numerator always gives the root.
It should be the square root of $x$, because the 3 cancels.
The denominator 3 gives the root, so it is the cube root of $x^{2}$.
It should be $x^{2}$ divided by 3, because the exponent is a fraction.
questions.answer: The denominator 3 gives the root, so it is the cube root of $x^{2}$.
questions.solution: In $x^{\frac{m}{n}}$ the denominator $n$ is the root and the numerator $m$ is the power, so $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x^{2}$.

solve.answer: The denominator 3 gives the root, so it is the cube root of $x^{2}$.
solve.work: x^(m/n) = nth root of x^m; x^(2/3) = cube root of x^2.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Why is $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$ equal to $\sqrt{x^{3}}$, for $x \ge 0$?
choices: Because $\frac{3}{2}$ is 1.5, so the expression is $x$ times 1.5.
Because the exponent $\frac{3}{2}$ means $x^{3}$ divided by 2.
Because the 3 tells which root to take, and the 2 tells the power.
questions.solution: Writing $\frac{3}{2} = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{2}$ gives $x^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(x^{3}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$, the square root of $x^{3}$.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Using $\left(a^{m}\right)^{n} = a^{mn}$: $\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)^{3} = x^{k}$ for $x > 0$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3} \cdot 3 = 2$, so $k = 2$. This shows $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x^{2}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: Written as a radical, $w^{\frac{5}{3}}$ is the cube root of $w^{k}$, for $w \ge 0$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The numerator of the exponent is the power under the root, so $k = 5$.

solve.work: w^{5/3} = cube root of w^5; k=5.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $0.09^{\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: $0.3 \cdot 0.3 = 0.09$, so the square root of 0.09 is 0.3.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: Rewrite $y^{\frac{3}{4}}$ as a radical expression, for $y \ge 0$. Which expression is correct?
choices: the fourth power of the cube root of $y$
questions.solution: The denominator 4 is the root and the numerator 3 is the power, so $y^{\frac{3}{4}}$ is the fourth root of $y^{3}$.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Using $\left(a^{m}\right)^{n} = a^{mn}$, which equation shows that $7^{\frac{1}{4}}$ is a fourth root of 7?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{1}{4} \cdot 4 = 1$. So $7^{\frac{1}{4}}$ used as a factor 4 times gives 7, which makes it the fourth root of 7.

solve.work: (7^(1/4))^4 = 7^(1/4*4) = 7^1 = 7, so 7^(1/4) raised to the 4th is 7: it is a fourth root.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $9^{\frac{1}{4}} \cdot 9^{\frac{1}{4}}$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$, so the product is $9^{\frac{1}{2}} = 3$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which pair of expressions is equal for every $x > 0$?
questions.solution: In $x^{\frac{2}{5}}$ the denominator 5 is the root and the numerator 2 is the power, so it equals the fifth root of $x^{2}$. The square root of $x^{5}$ is $x^{\frac{5}{2}}$.

solve.work: x^(2/5) = (x^2)^(1/5) = fifth root of x^2. Others: 2x/5 wrong, x^(5/2) is square root of x^5, x^(2/5) is not sqrt(x^5).

questions.skill: Find an unknown exponent or base
questions.stem: If $x^{\frac{1}{3}} = 4$, what is $x$?
questions.solution: Cube both sides: $x = 4^{3} = 64$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: A student rewrites $x^{\frac{3}{5}}$ for $x \ge 0$ in two steps, one a root and one a power. Which pair of steps is correct?
choices: Take the cube root, then raise the result to the fifth power.
Multiply $x$ by 3, then take the fifth root.
Take the fifth root, then cube the result.
questions.answer: Take the fifth root, then cube the result.
questions.solution: The denominator 5 gives the fifth root and the numerator 3 gives the cube: $x^{\frac{3}{5}} = \left(x^{\frac{1}{5}}\right)^{3}$.

solve.answer: Take the fifth root, then cube the result.
solve.work: x^(3/5) = (fifth root of x)^3: fifth root, then cube. Cube root then fifth power gives x^(5/3).

questions.skill: Find the error in a rewrite
questions.stem: Rosa writes $16^{\frac{1}{2}} = 8$. What mistake did Rosa make?
choices: She took the cube root of 16 instead of the square root.
She doubled 16 and then took half of the result.
She squared 16 instead of taking the root.
She halved 16 instead of taking the square root.
questions.answer: She halved 16 instead of taking the square root.
questions.solution: $16^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the square root of 16, which is 4, because $4 \cdot 4 = 16$. Rosa got 8 by computing $16 \div 2$.

solve.answer: She halved 16 instead of taking the square root.
solve.work: 16^(1/2) = 4. Rosa got 8 = 16/2: she halved 16 instead of taking the square root.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $27^{-\frac{2}{3}}$.
questions.solution: A negative exponent gives a reciprocal: $27^{-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{1}{27^{2/3}}$. The cube root of 27 is 3, and $3^2 = 9$, so the value is $\frac{1}{9}$.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: A student rewrites $x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ using a radical and no negative exponent, with $x > 0$. Which expression could the student write?
questions.solution: The negative sign in the exponent means a reciprocal, and $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root: $x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{16}{81}\right)^{\frac{3}{4}}$.
questions.solution: The fourth root of $\frac{16}{81}$ is $\frac{2}{3}$, since $2^4 = 16$ and $3^4 = 81$. Then $\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 = \frac{8}{27}$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\left(8x^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: Apply the exponent to each factor: $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$ and $\left(x^6\right)^{\frac{1}{3}} = x^2$. The result is $2x^2$.

questions.skill: Find an unknown exponent
questions.stem: If $64^{\frac{m}{6}} = 16$, what is $m$?
questions.solution: Write both sides with base 2: $64^{\frac{m}{6}} = \left(2^6\right)^{\frac{m}{6}} = 2^m$ and $16 = 2^4$. So $m = 4$.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: The negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = 4^{\frac{1}{2}}$, which is the square root of 4, or 2.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which statement is true for every positive $x$?
questions.solution: $\left(x^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^3 = x^{1} = x$ is true. The others are false: the first product is $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$, the second is $x^2$, and the sum is $2x^{\frac{1}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: A student wants to show that $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ means the cube root of $x$ and multiplies $x^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{3}}$. Which statement describes the result and what it shows?
choices: The product is $x^{\frac{1}{27}}$, so $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the twenty-seventh root of $x$.
The product is $x$, so using $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ as a factor three times gives $x$, like a cube root.
The product is $x^{\frac{1}{9}}$, so $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the ninth root of $x$ in this case.
The product is $x^{3}$, so $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the same as $x$ cubed in every case.
questions.answer: The product is $x$, so using $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ as a factor three times gives $x$, like a cube root.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = 1$, so the product is $x^1 = x$. A number that multiplies by itself three times to give $x$ is the cube root of $x$.

solve.answer: The product is $x$, so using $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$ as a factor three times gives $x$, like a cube root.
solve.work: x^(1/3+1/3+1/3) = x^1 = x. So x^(1/3) used as a factor three times gives x, matching the cube root.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, $\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)^{\frac{3}{4}} = x^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the product of the square root of $x$ and the cube root of $x$ equals $x^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: Write the roots as exponents and add: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $32^{\frac{3}{5}}$.
questions.solution: The fifth root of 32 is 2, since $2^{5} = 32$. Then $2^{3} = 8$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the expression $(2x)^{\frac{3}{2}}$ can be written as the square root of $kx^{3}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The numerator 3 is the power on the whole base $2x$: $(2x)^{3} = 8x^{3}$. The denominator 2 is the square root, so $k = 8$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: Which exponent expression equals the square root of $x$ times the fourth root of $x$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: Write each root as an exponent and add: $x^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{4}} = x^{\frac{2}{4} + \frac{1}{4}} = x^{\frac{3}{4}}$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent m/n to radical
questions.stem: Which radical expression is equal to $x^{0.75}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: Since $0.75 = \frac{3}{4}$, the expression is $x^{\frac{3}{4}}$, the fourth root of $x^{3}$.

solve.work: 0.75 = 3/4, so x^{3/4} = fourth root of x^3.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{25}{36}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: A negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{36}{25}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{6}{5}$.

questions.skill: Find an unknown exponent or base
questions.stem: If $9^{k} = 27$, what is $k$?
questions.solution: Write both as powers of 3: $9^{k} = 3^{2k}$ and $27 = 3^{3}$. So $2k = 3$ and $k = \frac{3}{2}$.

questions.skill: Find an unknown exponent or base
questions.stem: If $x^{\frac{3}{2}} = 27$ and $x > 0$, what is $x$?
questions.solution: Raise both sides to the power $\frac{2}{3}$: $x = 27^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(27^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{2} = 3^{2} = 9$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, $\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{3} \cdot \sqrt{x} = x^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: $\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{3} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}$. Multiplying by $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$ adds the exponents: $\frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 2$.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Let $y = x^{\frac{3}{5}}$ for $x > 0$. Then $y^{5} = x^{k}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: $y^{5} = \left(x^{\frac{3}{5}}\right)^{5} = x^{3}$, so $k = 3$. This shows $y$ is the fifth root of $x^{3}$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(8^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot 8^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{3}$.
questions.solution: $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$, so the inside is $2 \cdot 2 = 4$, and $4^{3} = 64$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which of these simplifications is correct when $x \ge 0$?

solve.work: sqrt(x^3) = sqrt(x^2 * x) = x sqrt(x) for x >= 0. (sqrt x)^2 = x, x^3/2 wrong.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^{3}}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{x^{3}} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}$, and the reciprocal of $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$ is $x^{-\frac{3}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Find an unknown exponent or base
questions.stem: For what whole number $n$ is $64^{\frac{1}{n}} = 2$?
questions.solution: $2^{6} = 64$, so 2 is the sixth root of 64 and $n = 6$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $0.04^{\frac{3}{2}}$. Give the answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: The square root of 0.04 is 0.2, and $0.2^{3} = 0.008$.

questions.skill: Simplify with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\left(\frac{x^{4}}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Take the fourth root of top and bottom: $\left(x^{4}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}} = x$ and $16^{\frac{1}{4}} = 2$.

questions.skill: Radical to rational exponent
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the cube root of the square root of $x$ equals $x^{p}$. What is $p$?
questions.solution: The square root is $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$. Its cube root is $\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}} = x^{\frac{1}{6}}$, so $p = \frac{1}{6}$.

questions.skill: Negative rational exponent
questions.stem: In a model, the pressure of a gas is $P = V^{-\frac{3}{4}}$, where $V$ is the volume in liters. What is $P$ when $V = 81$?

questions.skill: Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Which calculation correctly finds the value of $27^{\frac{4}{3}}$?
questions.solution: The cube root of 27 is 3, and then $3^{4} = 81$.

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent forms
questions.stem: Which value or expression is NOT equal to $16^{\frac{3}{4}}$?
questions.solution: The fourth root of 16 is 2, and $2^{3} = 8$. The fourth root of $16^{3} = 4096$ is also 8, as is the cube of 2. Only 12 is different.

solve.work: 16^(3/4) = 2^3 = 8. Cube of 2 = 8; fourth root of 4096 = 8 (8^4 = 4096). 12 is not equal.

questions.skill: Why a rational exponent is a root
questions.stem: Which statement correctly explains why $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the cube root of $x^{2}$, for $x > 0$?
choices: Multiplying it by itself twice gives $x^{\frac{2}{9}}$.
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents when raising a power to a power: $\frac{2}{3} \cdot 3 = 2$. So $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ is the number whose cube is $x^{2}$, the cube root of $x^{2}$.

solve.work: (x^(2/3))^3 = x^(2/3*3) = x^2, so x^(2/3) is the number whose cube is x^2.

questions.skill: Evaluate a unit-fraction exponent
Evaluate an m/n exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$.
questions.solution: The square root of $\frac{9}{4}$ is $\frac{3}{2}$, and $\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{3} = \frac{27}{8}$.

questions.skill: Find the error in a rewrite
questions.stem: A student simplifies $\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$ as $x^{\frac{5}{6}}$. What is the error, and what is the correct result?
choices: The exponents should be multiplied, giving $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$.
The exponents should be divided, giving $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$.
The exponents should be multiplied, giving $x^{6}$.
There is no error, because a power of a power adds the exponents.
questions.answer: The exponents should be multiplied, giving $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$.
questions.solution: A power raised to a power multiplies the exponents: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{6}$. This is the sixth root of $x$.

solve.answer: The exponents should be multiplied, giving $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$.
solve.work: Power of a power multiplies exponents: (1/2)(1/3)=1/6, x^(1/6). Student added (1/2+1/3=5/6).

questions.skill: Rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$ for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, so $x^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{x}$. Squaring, halving and taking a reciprocal are different operations.

solve.work: x^{1/2} is the principal square root of x for x >= 0.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $49^{\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, and the square root of 49 is 7.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Mia knows that $a^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the cube root of $a$. What is $a^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when $a = 125$?
questions.solution: The cube root of 125 is the number that multiplies by itself three times to give 125. Since $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$, the answer is 5.

questions.skill: Rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which expression is the cube root of $x$ written with an exponent?
questions.solution: The cube root is the exponent $\frac{1}{3}$, so the cube root of $x$ is $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$. The exponent 3 would cube $x$ instead.

solve.work: The cube root of x is x^{1/3}.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Multiplying powers of the same base adds their exponents. For $x > 0$, the product $x^{\frac{1}{4}} \cdot x^{\frac{3}{4}}$ is written as $x^{n}$. What is the value of $n$?
questions.solution: When powers of the same base are multiplied, the exponents are added: $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{4} = 1$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: Simplify $\left(x^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$, where $x > 0$. What is the result?
questions.solution: For a power of a power, multiply the exponents: $2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 1$, so the result is $x^{1} = x$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: What is $\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{8}$?
questions.solution: Multiply under the radical: $\sqrt{2 \cdot 8} = \sqrt{16} = 4$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\sqrt{12}$?
questions.solution: Write $12 = 4 \cdot 3$. Then $\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{4}\cdot\sqrt{3} = 2\sqrt{3}$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: What is $3\sqrt{5} + 2\sqrt{5}$?
questions.solution: The radicals are alike, so add the coefficients: $3 + 2 = 5$. The radical stays $\sqrt{5}$, giving $5\sqrt{5}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $16^{\frac{1}{4}}$?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{4}$ means the fourth root. Since $2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 16$, the fourth root of 16 is 2.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: A square has an area of 45 square centimeters, so its side is $\sqrt{45}$ centimeters. This equals $3\sqrt{n}$ centimeters. What is $n$?
questions.solution: $45 = 9 \cdot 5$, so $\sqrt{45} = \sqrt{9}\cdot\sqrt{5} = 3\sqrt{5}$. Thus $n = 5$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 343 cubic inches. What is its edge length, in inches? (The edge is $343^{\frac{1}{3}}$.)
questions.solution: $7 \times 7 \times 7 = 343$, so the cube root of 343 is 7.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the expression $\left(x^{8}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}$ equals $x^{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents: $8 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 2$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: Which is $\sqrt{50}$ in simplest radical form?
questions.solution: $50 = 25 \cdot 2$, so $\sqrt{50} = \sqrt{25}\cdot\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: What is $7\sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}$?
questions.solution: The radicals are like terms, so subtract the coefficients and keep $\sqrt{2}$: $(7 - 3)\sqrt{2} = 4\sqrt{2}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A square garden has an area of 121 square feet. Writing its side as $121^{\frac{1}{2}}$ feet, how many feet long is the side?
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, and the square root of 121 is 11.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: Maya checks four equations that use fraction exponents. Which equation is correct?
questions.solution: The exponent $\frac{1}{2}$ means the square root, and $\sqrt{100} = 10$. The others are wrong: $81^{\frac{1}{4}} = 3$ (not $81 \div 4$) and $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$ (not 4), and $100^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is not $100 \div 2$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: Which of these radicals is already in simplest form?
questions.solution: $15 = 3 \cdot 5$ has no perfect-square factor larger than 1. The others simplify: $\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$, $\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}$.

solve.work: 18=9*2, 20=4*5, 27=9*3 have square factors; 15=3*5 has none, so sqrt15 is simplest.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: The sum $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}$ can be written as $a\sqrt{2}$. What is $a$?
questions.solution: Three copies of $\sqrt{2}$ make $3\sqrt{2}$, so $a = 3$.

questions.skill: Convert between rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: For $x \ge 0$, the expression $x^{\frac{3}{2}}$ equals the square root of $x^{m}$. What is $m$?
questions.solution: The denominator 2 is the square root and the numerator 3 is the power inside it, so $x^{\frac{3}{2}} = \sqrt{x^{3}}$ and $m = 3$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the quotient $\dfrac{x^{\frac{5}{2}}}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}$ equals $x^{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: When dividing powers of the same base, subtract the exponents: $\frac{5}{2} - \frac{3}{2} = 1$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent
questions.stem: The cube root of 8 is 2. Use this to find $8^{\frac{4}{3}}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression equals $x^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{3}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents: $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent
questions.stem: Which of these expressions equals 8?
questions.solution: $4^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{4}\right)^{3} = 2^{3} = 8$. The others are 4, 4 and 27.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 216 cubic centimeters. Its edge length is $216^{\frac{1}{3}}$ centimeters. How long is each edge, in centimeters?
questions.solution: An exponent of $\frac{1}{3}$ means the cube root. Since $6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216$, the edge is 6 centimeters.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: A rectangle has a width of $\sqrt{3}$ centimeters and a length of $\sqrt{27}$ centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area $= \sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{27} = \sqrt{81} = 9$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: What is the value of $100^{-\frac{1}{2}}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $100^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{100^{\frac{1}{2}}} = \frac{1}{10}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Dana knows that $125^{-\frac{1}{3}}$ is the reciprocal of $125^{\frac{1}{3}}$. What is the value of $125^{-\frac{1}{3}}$?
questions.solution: $125^{\frac{1}{3}} = 5$, because $5^3 = 125$. The reciprocal of 5 is $\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression equals $\left(y^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{4}$, for $y > 0$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 = 2$, so the result is $y^{2}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Use exponent rules to evaluate $9^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot 9^{\frac{1}{2}}$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1$, so the product is $9^{1} = 9$.

questions.skill: Convert between rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the expression $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$ is the $n$th root of $x$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: The denominator of a unit-fraction exponent names the root. Since $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$ has denominator 6, it is the 6th root of $x$, so $n = 6$.

solve.work: x^(1/6) is the sixth root. n=6.

questions.skill: Rewrite a radical expression with a variable
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x}$, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\cdot x^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^{1} = x$.

questions.skill: Convert between rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which is the cube root of $x^{2}$ written with a rational exponent, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: The root index (3) goes in the denominator and the power (2) in the numerator, so the cube root of $x^{2}$ is $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent
questions.stem: What is $9^{\frac{3}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The denominator 2 is the square root and the numerator 3 is the power: $\left(\sqrt{9}\right)^{3} = 3^{3} = 27$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $8^{\frac{2}{3}}$.
questions.solution: Take the cube root first, then square: $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$ and $2^{2} = 4$.

questions.skill: Rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which radical expression matches $x^{\frac{3}{4}}$ when $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: In $x^{\frac{m}{n}}$ the denominator $n$ is the root and the numerator $m$ is the power. Here $n = 4$ and $m = 3$, so it is the fourth root of $x^{3}$. The cube root of $x^{4}$ would be $x^{\frac{4}{3}}$.

solve.work: x^{m/n} = nth root of x^m, so x^{3/4} = fourth root of x^3.

questions.skill: Rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which is $\sqrt{x^{5}}$ written with a rational exponent, for $x \ge 0$?
questions.solution: A square root is the exponent $\frac{1}{2}$, so $\sqrt{x^{5}} = \left(x^{5}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^{5 \cdot \frac{1}{2}} = x^{\frac{5}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which single power of $x$ is the product $x^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{6}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{4}{6} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: A student simplifies $\left(x^{\frac{3}{4}}\right)^{4}$ for $x > 0$ and gets a single power of $x$. What is the exponent?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{3}{4} \cdot 4 = 3$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: The number $\sqrt{72}$ can be written as $a\sqrt{2}$, where $a$ is a whole number. What is $a$?
questions.solution: Write $72 = 36 \cdot 2$. Then $\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36}\cdot\sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}$, so $a = 6$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to the cube root of 54?
questions.solution: Write $54 = 27 \cdot 2$. The cube root of 27 is 3, so the cube root of 54 is 3 times the cube root of 2.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\sqrt{8} + \sqrt{18}$?
questions.solution: Simplify each radical: $\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}$ and $\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$. They are alike, so $2\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}$. Radicals cannot be added by adding what is under them.

solve.work: sqrt8 = 2 sqrt2, sqrt18 = 3 sqrt2; sum 5 sqrt2. (5 sqrt4 = 10, sqrt26 ~ 5.10, 6 sqrt2 ~ 8.49 are not equal to ~7.07.)

questions.solution: $\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}$ and $\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$, so the difference is $2\sqrt{3}$ and $a = 2$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Tom rewrites $8^{-\frac{2}{3}}$ as a single fraction. What fraction does he get?
questions.solution: $8^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\text{cube root of } 8\right)^{2} = 2^{2} = 4$. The negative exponent makes it a reciprocal, so $8^{-\frac{2}{3}} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Which expression equals $\dfrac{x^{\frac{3}{4}}}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{4} - \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Convert between rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{3}}}$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{x^{3}} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}$, and dividing 1 by it gives the negative exponent: $x^{-\frac{3}{2}}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Use exponent rules to evaluate $5^{\frac{1}{3}} \cdot 5^{\frac{5}{3}}$.
questions.solution: Add the exponents: $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{5}{3} = 2$, so the product is $5^{2} = 25$.

questions.solution: The root of a product is the product of the roots. A root of a sum is not the sum of roots: for example $\sqrt{1 + 1} \ne 1 + 1$.

questions.solution: $36^{\frac{1}{2}} = 6$, $216^{\frac{1}{3}} = 6$ and $9^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot 4^{\frac{1}{2}} = 3 \cdot 2 = 6$. But $36^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is the cube root of 36, which is not 6.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{-\frac{3}{4}}$.
questions.solution: The negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{-\frac{3}{4}} = 16^{\frac{3}{4}}$. The fourth root of 16 is 2, and $2^{3} = 8$.

questions.solution: Since $\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, the reciprocal $\frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}$ is $x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, so $n = -\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent

questions.solution: The cube root of $\frac{8}{27}$ is $\frac{2}{3}$, and squaring gives $\frac{4}{9}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Evaluate $\dfrac{2^{\frac{5}{2}}}{2^{\frac{1}{2}}}$.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $\frac{5}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = 2$, so the value is $2^{2} = 4$.

questions.skill: Simplify a radical
questions.stem: A student writes $\sqrt{48x^{3}}$, with $x > 0$, in simplest radical form. What does the student get?
questions.solution: Pull out the perfect squares: $48x^{3} = 16x^{2} \cdot 3x$. Then $\sqrt{48x^{3}} = 4x\sqrt{3x}$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: Written in simplest form, the cube root of $8x^{6}$ is which expression, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Apply the exponent to each factor: $8^{\frac{1}{3}} = 2$ and $\left(x^{6}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}} = x^{2}$, so the result is $2x^{2}$.

solve.work: cube root of 8 = 2, cube root of x^6 = x^2; 2x^2.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals

questions.solution: Distribute: $\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{36} = 6$ and $\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{27} = \sqrt{81} = 9$. The sum is 15.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: A rectangle has a width of $\sqrt{6}$ centimeters and an area of $\sqrt{150}$ square centimeters. What is its length, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Length = area divided by width $= \sqrt{150} \div \sqrt{6} = \sqrt{25} = 5$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the expression $\left(x^{\frac{4}{3}}\right)^{-\frac{3}{2}}$ equals $x^{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $\frac{4}{3} \cdot \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -2$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: What is the value of $\left(\sqrt{7} + \sqrt{3}\right)\left(\sqrt{7} - \sqrt{3}\right)$?
questions.solution: The middle terms cancel, leaving $\left(\sqrt{7}\right)^{2} - \left(\sqrt{3}\right)^{2} = 7 - 3 = 4$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a rational exponent
questions.stem: A culture has $50 \cdot 8^{\frac{t}{3}}$ cells after $t$ hours. How many cells are there after 2 hours?
questions.solution: $8^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\text{cube root of } 8\right)^{2} = 4$, so there are $50 \cdot 4 = 200$ cells.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: Which expression equals $\sqrt{75} + \sqrt{12} - \sqrt{27}$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$ and $\sqrt{27} = 3\sqrt{3}$. Then $5 + 2 - 3 = 4$, giving $4\sqrt{3}$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Evaluate $81^{-\frac{3}{4}}$ and write the answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The 4th root of 81 is 3, so $81^{\frac{3}{4}} = 3^{3} = 27$. The negative exponent gives the reciprocal, $\frac{1}{27}$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: The number $3\sqrt{2}$ can be written as a single square root, $\sqrt{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: Move the 3 under the root by squaring it: $3\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{9}\cdot\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{18}$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: Simplify $\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{6}}\right)^{2}$ for $x > 0$.
questions.solution: Inside the parentheses add the exponents: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. Then raise to the power 2 by multiplying: $\frac{5}{6} \cdot 2 = \frac{5}{3}$.

questions.skill: Rewrite a radical expression with a variable
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the expression $\dfrac{\sqrt{50x^{3}}}{\sqrt{2x}}$ equals $ax$. What is $a$?
questions.solution: Combine under one root: $\sqrt{\frac{50x^{3}}{2x}} = \sqrt{25x^{2}} = 5x$, so $a = 5$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a unit-fraction exponent
questions.stem: A cube has a volume of 729 cubic inches, so each edge is $729^{\frac{1}{3}}$ inches. What is the area of one face, in square inches?
questions.solution: The cube root of 729 is 9, so each edge is 9 inches. One face is a 9 by 9 square, with area $9^2 = 81$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: What is the value of $\left(\frac{9}{25}\right)^{-\frac{3}{2}}$?
questions.solution: The negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{25}{9}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$. The square root of $\frac{25}{9}$ is $\frac{5}{3}$, and cubing gives $\frac{125}{27}$.

questions.skill: Convert between rational exponent and radical form
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, which expression is NOT equal to $x^{\frac{3}{4}}$?
questions.solution: $\left(x^{4}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}} = x^{\frac{4}{3}}$, which is a different power. The other three all mean the 4th root with the power 3.

questions.skill: Evaluate a power with a negative rational exponent
questions.stem: Which number equals $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}$?
questions.solution: The negative exponent flips the fraction: $8^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\text{cube root of } 8\right)^{2} = 2^{2} = 4$.

questions.skill: Rewrite a radical expression with a variable
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, which is the cube root of $24x^{4}$ in simplest form?
questions.solution: $24x^{4} = 8x^{3} \cdot 3x$. The cube root of $8x^{3}$ is $2x$, and the cube root of $3x$ stays inside the radical.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: Dividing $x^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{3}{4}}$ by $x^{\frac{1}{6}}$ gives which power of $x$, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Add the exponents in the numerator: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{17}{12}$. Subtract the exponent below: $\frac{17}{12} - \frac{2}{12} = \frac{15}{12} = \frac{5}{4}$.

questions.skill: Decide which radical or exponent statements are true
questions.stem: Ana tests four equations with fraction exponents. Which one holds for every $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Multiplying powers adds the exponents: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = 1$, so the product is $x$. In the other three, the exponents are wrongly multiplied (giving $x^{\frac{2}{9}}$ twice) or subtracted (giving $x^{\frac{1}{3}}$), so none equals $x$.

questions.skill: Power of a power with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, which expression equals the square root of the square root of $x$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{\sqrt{x}} = \left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^{\frac{1}{4}}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the expression $\dfrac{x^{-\frac{1}{2}} \cdot x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{x^{\frac{1}{4}}}$ equals $x^{n}$. What is $n$? Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Add in the numerator: $-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{2} = 1$. Then subtract the bottom exponent: $1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Add, subtract and multiply radicals
questions.stem: What is the value of $3\sqrt{6} \cdot 2\sqrt{24}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the outside numbers: $3 \cdot 2 = 6$. Multiply the radicals: $\sqrt{6}\cdot\sqrt{24} = \sqrt{144} = 12$. So the product is $6 \cdot 12 = 72$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the cube root of $x$ divided by the square root of $x$ equals $x^{n}$. What is $n$? Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{6} - \frac{3}{6} = -\frac{1}{6}$.

questions.skill: Product and quotient of powers with rational exponents
questions.stem: The square root of $x$ times the cube root of $x$ equals which expression, for $x > 0$?
questions.solution: Write each root as a power: $x^{\frac{1}{2}} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{3}} = x^{\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}} = x^{\frac{5}{6}}$.

questions.skill: Decide which radical or exponent statements are true
questions.stem: A student simplifies $\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}$ for $x > 0$ and writes $x^{\frac{13}{6}}$. What mistake did the student make?
choices: The student added the exponents instead of multiplying them
The student multiplied the exponents instead of adding them
The student divided the exponents instead of multiplying them
The student subtracted the exponents instead of multiplying them
questions.answer: The student added the exponents instead of multiplying them
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{13}{6}$, so the student added. A power of a power needs the exponents multiplied: $\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 1$, giving $x$.

solve.answer: The student added the exponents instead of multiplying them
solve.work: Correct: (2/3)(3/2) = 1, x^1. Student got 13/6 = 2/3 + 3/2: added instead of multiplying.

questions.solution: The sum of two rational numbers is rational: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{4}$. In each other sum, one number is irrational and the other is rational, so the sum is irrational.

solve.work: 1/2 + 3/4 = 5/4 rational; the others include an irrational plus a rational.

questions.skill: rational plus irrational

questions.solution: $\sqrt{5}$ is irrational, and a rational number plus an irrational number is irrational. The other three are made only from rational numbers, so each is rational.

questions.skill: classify a number as rational or irrational

questions.solution: $\frac{1}{3} \cdot 6 = 2$ is rational. $\sqrt{2} \cdot 5$ is a nonzero rational times an irrational, so it is irrational. $\pi + 1$ is irrational. $4 + 0.2 = 4.2$ is rational. So 2 are irrational.

solve.work: (1/3)*6 = 2 rational; 5*sqrt2 irrational; pi + 1 irrational; 4.2 rational. Two irrational.

questions.skill: sum of rationals

questions.solution: Write the numbers as fractions $\frac{a}{b}$ and $\frac{c}{d}$. Their sum $\frac{ad + bc}{bd}$ is again a ratio of integers, so it is always rational.

solve.work: a/b + c/d = (ad+bc)/(bd), a ratio of integers with nonzero denominator: always rational.

questions.skill: product of rationals
questions.stem: Find the product $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{4}$ as a fraction in lowest terms.
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{4} = \frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}$. The product of two rational numbers is a rational number.

questions.skill: rational plus irrational

questions.solution: A rational number (3) plus an irrational number ($\sqrt{2}$) is always irrational. So $3 + \sqrt{2}$ is irrational and its decimal never ends or repeats.

solve.work: Rational 3 plus irrational sqrt2 is irrational.

questions.skill: classify a number as rational or irrational

questions.skill: sum of rationals

questions.skill: nonzero rational times irrational
questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 3 meters, so its circumference is $3\pi$ meters. What can be said about the circumference?
choices: It is rational, because the diameter 3 is a rational number.
It is irrational, because a nonzero rational times an irrational is irrational.
It is rational, because the product of any two real numbers is always a rational number.
It is irrational, because 3 is a whole number greater than 1.
questions.answer: It is irrational, because a nonzero rational times an irrational is irrational.
questions.solution: The diameter 3 is a nonzero rational number and $\pi$ is irrational. A nonzero rational number times an irrational number is irrational, so $3\pi$ is irrational.

solve.answer: It is irrational, because a nonzero rational times an irrational is irrational.
solve.work: 3 is a nonzero rational and pi is irrational, so 3pi is irrational.

questions.skill: zero times an irrational
questions.stem: What is the value of $0 \times \pi$?
questions.solution: Anything times 0 is 0. So $0 \times \pi = 0$, which is a rational number even though $\pi$ is irrational.

questions.skill: Rational plus irrational
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: A rational number plus an irrational number is always rational.
The sum of two rational numbers is always an irrational number.
The product of two rational numbers is always an irrational number.
A rational number plus an irrational number is always irrational.
questions.answer: A rational number plus an irrational number is always irrational.
questions.solution: If the sum were a rational number $q$, then the irrational number would equal $q$ minus a rational, which is rational. That is impossible, so the sum is irrational. Sums and products of two rationals are rational.

solve.answer: A rational number plus an irrational number is always irrational.

questions.solution: $\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{n}$ is rational only when $\sqrt{n}$ is rational, that is, when $n$ is a perfect square. The perfect squares from 1 to 20 are 1, 4, 9 and 16. The other $20-4=16$ numbers give an irrational result.

solve.work: (3/5)sqrt n rational only when n is a perfect square: 1,4,9,16. 20 - 4 = 16.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: Which statement about $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{8}$ is correct?
choices: It is irrational, because both factors are irrational.
It is rational, because the product simplifies to 4.
It is irrational, because it equals $\sqrt{10}$.
It is rational, because $\sqrt{8}$ is a whole number.
questions.answer: It is rational, because the product simplifies to 4.
questions.solution: $\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{8} = \sqrt{16} = 4$, a rational number. So the product of two irrational numbers can be rational.

solve.answer: It is rational, because the product simplifies to 4.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: Which pair of irrational numbers has a rational sum?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{2} + (-\sqrt{2}) = 0$, which is rational. The sums $\pi + 2\pi = 3\pi$ and $\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{5} + 1 = 2\sqrt{5} + 1$ are irrational, and $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}$ is irrational too.

solve.work: sqrt2 + (-sqrt2) = 0 rational. sqrt2+sqrt3 irrational; pi+2pi = 3pi irrational; sqrt5 + sqrt5 + 1 = 2sqrt5 + 1 irrational.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: Let $x = 4 + \sqrt{6}$ and $y = 1 - \sqrt{6}$. Both are irrational. What is $x + y$?
questions.solution: $x + y = 4 + \sqrt{6} + 1 - \sqrt{6} = 5$. The $\sqrt{6}$ terms cancel, so the sum of these two irrational numbers is rational.

questions.skill: explaining why (reasons and proof)
questions.stem: Suppose $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}$ were a rational number $q$. Which statement gives the contradiction?
choices: Then $\sqrt{2} = \frac{2}{3}q$ would be irrational, so $q$ must be irrational as well, and nothing is wrong.
Then $q$ would equal $\sqrt{2}$, which is a whole number, and this is impossible.
Then $\frac{2}{3}$ would have to be irrational, since $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
Then $\sqrt{2} = \frac{3}{2}q$ would be rational, as a product of rationals, but $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
questions.answer: Then $\sqrt{2} = \frac{3}{2}q$ would be rational, as a product of rationals, but $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
questions.solution: If $q = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}$, multiplying by $\frac{3}{2}$ gives $\sqrt{2} = \frac{3}{2}q$. A product of two rational numbers is rational, but $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational. So $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}$ is not rational.

solve.answer: Then $\sqrt{2} = \frac{3}{2}q$ would be rational, as a product of rationals, but $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
solve.work: If (2/3)sqrt2 = q then sqrt2 = (3/2)q, a product of rationals, so rational: contradiction.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: What is the value of $(4 + \sqrt{7})(4 - \sqrt{7})$?
questions.solution: Using $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$: $4^2 - (\sqrt{7})^2 = 16 - 7 = 9$. The product of these two irrational numbers is rational.

questions.skill: classify a number as rational or irrational
questions.stem: How many of the five numbers $\sqrt{12} \cdot \sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{2} + 4$, $(1 + \sqrt{5}) + (1 - \sqrt{5})$, $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\frac{7}{3} \cdot 0$ are rational?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{12} \cdot \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{36} = 6$ is rational. $\sqrt{2} + 4$ is irrational. $(1 + \sqrt{5}) + (1 - \sqrt{5}) = 2$ is rational. $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2}$ is irrational. $\frac{7}{3} \cdot 0 = 0$ is rational. So 3 are rational.

solve.work: sqrt12*sqrt3 = sqrt36 = 6 rational; sqrt2 + 4 irrational; (1+sqrt5)+(1-sqrt5) = 2 rational; sqrt2/2 irrational; (7/3)*0 = 0 rational. Three rational.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: Which example shows that the statement "the product of two irrational numbers is irrational" is false?
questions.solution: A counterexample needs two irrational numbers whose product is rational. $\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 3$ does that. In the other examples the product is irrational, or one of the factors (5 or 1) is not irrational.

solve.work: A counterexample needs two irrationals with rational product: sqrt3*sqrt3 = 3.

questions.skill: nonzero rational times irrational
questions.stem: The numbers $a$ and $b$ are rational and $b \ne 0$. Which expression must be irrational?
questions.solution: $b\sqrt{2}$ is a nonzero rational times an irrational, so it is irrational. Adding the rational number $a$ keeps it irrational. The other three are built from rational numbers only, so they are rational.

solve.work: b nonzero rational, so b*sqrt2 irrational; a + irrational is irrational. The others are rational.

questions.skill: sums and products of two irrationals
questions.stem: A rectangle has length $\sqrt{18}$ cm and width $\sqrt{8}$ cm. Its area is a rational number. What is the area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = $\sqrt{18} \times \sqrt{8} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ square centimeters. Check: $\sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$ and $\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}$, so the product is $6 \cdot 2 = 12$.

questions.skill: explaining why (reasons and proof)
questions.stem: Which statement is false?
choices: The sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
The sum of a rational number and another rational number is rational.
The product of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
The product of a rational number and another rational number is rational.
questions.answer: The product of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
questions.solution: The statement about the product is false: $0 \times \sqrt{2} = 0$ is rational, and the rule needs the rational number to be nonzero. The other three statements are always true.

solve.answer: The product of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
solve.work: B fails when the rational is 0 (0 times an irrational is 0). A, C, D are true.
